assessment_scope: Targeted source inventory through WU-010 additive lifecycle contract compatibility. Prior unaffected classifications are carried forward; new transaction v2 schemas, reference converter and descriptor mapping do not establish runtime publication or full product acceptance. WU-004 native rename erratum records a candidate API correction; classifications are unchanged and WU-006 qualification remains open. WU-006 revision 4 admits named service, build, lifecycle, policy and profile paths. Disposable candidates now cover native no-replace rename, same-handle identity/security observation, token facts, protected descriptor construction, and parent-bound create-only anchor creation; the qualified publisher remains absent. A further disposable read-only candidate observes held-handle local NTFS facts and exact file/directory stream shape; it does not change publisher classification. A read-only candidate now enumerates held-directory descendants, reopens them relative to retained parents, and records bounded identity/content digests; protected security and multi-phase publication remain absent. The read-only tree candidate now carries same-handle file/directory owner and DACL facts, compares independent phase observations, and checks an exact protected descriptor shape; no service-bound or effective-right qualification is claimed. A held destination-parent wrapper now derives the exact visible-root name and reopens the listed child against the sealed tree; parent-chain protection and publication remain unqualified. A further read-only candidate binds exact directory chains from held parent handles and compares fresh phases; the volume-root boundary, sibling anchor roles, service and effective rights remain unqualified. A read-only candidate now binds four sibling anchor roles under a held directory chain and corroborates a named own-process restricted SCM service with current process-token facts. The ordinary-user fixture only proves refusal for an absent service; no installed target or publisher qualification exists. WU-005 follow-up records one completed 2 GiB streamed install/verify and planning-only 4,096-entry child-process peaks; full ceiling lifecycle and release acceptance remain open. A further WU-005 legacy-record probe prepares prior-format records outside the measured child, then separately measures verify and uninstall planning at 128, 4,097 and 8,192 one-byte files; it does not establish an aggregate report budget. A WU-006 file-creation candidate now creates regular staged files relative to a held parent with a creation-time descriptor; local ordinary-user tests cover canonical names and collision/substitution refusal. This is not protected staging or a qualified publisher. WU-012 through WU-018 now permit only the exact generated inventory output after implementation changes; this scope correction does not change implementation classifications. WU-012 now has a bounded source-level authoring compiler for a selected target, deterministic unsigned ZIP/sidecar output, exact byte inventory and reopening checks; this is not a machine plan, setup application, signed package, or acceptance-qualified release. The integrated WU-012 source receipt and exact top-level CMakeLists.txt scope correction for WU-013 through WU-018 change no product qualification or requirement classification. WU-013 adds a source-level one-shot read-only machine command host with bounded JSON/framed input and explicit request-file mode; broader human CLI, stateful transport, reconnection and full acceptance remain open. WU-005 revision 4 admits only the ownership reader implementation file for measured legacy-record memory work; no memory ceiling or product qualification changes in this scope correction. WU-005 legacy ownership and report digest paths now stream canonical hashing; selected 8,192-entry ordinary-user peaks fall below a 64 MiB comparison ceiling, while full lifecycle and release qualification remain open. WU-014 now composes a Windows x64 inspect-only bundle envelope with sidecar and deterministic one-file ZIP carrier shapes; neither profile is an install-capable setup or release-qualified dependency closure. WU-006 revision 5 admits only the exact CI workflow file for ephemeral Windows lab probes; no publisher qualification or requirement classification changes.
release_scope: selected: Universal Setup 1.1 train targeting 1.1.0 Local Setup Foundation; exact support and release readiness not established
working_tree_note: Assessment source includes WU-010 implementation 60efbe0400c85f37b1935fc387801209f452932f and WU-006 candidate source. WU-004/005 integrated receipts are present. Published transaction v1 operation enums remain closed; v2 is additive and the reference converter has no execution authority. WU-005 retains its 24-case Windows NTFS memory matrix and 4,097-file prior-format verification fixture; STREAM-001 now has one completed 2 GiB streamed install/verify and 4,096-entry planning-only peaks. Full ceiling lifecycle, wider multi-gigabyte corpus and legacy-report acceptance remain partial. A clean-source Windows NTFS Debug matrix measured prior-format verify/uninstall planning in fresh children at 128, 4,097 and 8,192 files after separate fixture preparation; 8,192-file verify peaked at 97,431,552 bytes, above the 64 MiB comparison threshold, and no aggregate report budget is enforced. WU-006 revision 4 admits named file families while contracts, release records and other specification files remain read-only. Local Windows 10 build 19045 C: NTFS fixtures passed no-replace/substitution probes, same-handle owner/DACL reobservation, token/impersonation observations, protected descriptor shape, and parent-bound create-only/collision observations. The descriptor test is in memory; the create probe uses a disposable ordinary-user descriptor, not a restricted service. No installed restricted service, dedicated protected volume, complete closure, durable recovery, crash qualification, or production publication success is included. OD-001 and wider lifecycle/authoring acceptance remain open. A later ordinary-user C: NTFS fixture observed the handle-bound volume tuple, one unnamed file data stream, empty directory stream enumeration, and rejection of named streams on files and directories. This is not a dedicated protected volume or complete closure qualification. A local ordinary-user Windows 10 build 19045 C: NTFS fixture exercised 640-file directory pagination, exact native parent/name and listed/reopened 128-bit ID binding, nested digest observation, hard-link and named-stream refusal. A directory listing size was stale while a writer remained open; the candidate uses the reopened file handle for size and content. This is not an admitted protected target, complete security closure, durable publication, or recovery proof. Additional ordinary-user C: NTFS tests observed a descendant DACL protection change and a root rename across fresh tree phases; a synthetic exact descriptor tree passes the shape predicate while the real ordinary-user tree refuses. A held destination-parent wrapper derives the exact visible name and reopens the listed child; a local fixture verified handle binding after parent-path substitution. The parent chain is not qualified as protected. No installed restricted service or effective-right attack harness was used. A local ordinary-user 12-level directory-chain fixture with 64 sibling files per level passed; the observer releases each full sibling listing before descending, rechecks held parents, and rejects forged disconnected paths, duplicate identities, noncanonical components and changed DACL facts. This does not establish the dedicated protected volume-root boundary or a complete publisher. A local ordinary-user anchor fixture reobserved staging, destination-parent, state and journal sibling roles and refused duplicate IDs, case-fold name collisions, DACL drift and ordinary-user protected shape. A local token fixture refused an absent/malformed named service; no installed restricted publisher service positive observation was run. The second anchor enumeration detects stable name substitution between scans, not an atomic snapshot or hostile concurrent-race exclusion. A parent-bound file primitive passed a disposable local Windows Debug probe for write/flush, canonical Unicode and 129-unit names, create-only collision, and held-parent path substitution. Independent source review found no blocker for this partial candidate; OD-001 and strict production refusal remain open. Exact inventory-output scope was admitted for WU-012 through WU-018 with task revisions and regenerated specification seal; no product behavior or acceptance is claimed by this correction. The specification self-test fixture cleanup now retries only transient ENOTEMPTY from its disposable Git repository after two hosted specification jobs observed that race; persistent cleanup errors still fail. A WU-012 compiler reads declared finalized files without hooks, emits deterministic stored ZIP bytes and a sidecar retaining component choices, then reopens and hashes every entry. Focused tests cover graph alternatives, hostile paths/collisions, tampering and an independently compiled one-file executable from a separate project root. The source-open checks do not qualify hostile concurrent source swaps; no native lifecycle integration, full target matrix or signed carrier exists. A later source review found and repaired a file-as-parent collision hidden by an interposed sibling name, and an overlong path component accepted for a Windows target; both compile and inspect paths now reject the affected cases. Cleanup also preserves a file created by another writer after exclusive-create collision. WU-012 source head fcfd257bb64af4cd8ed55c0cc4baae6c35229632 merged through PR 88 with two successful exact-head CI runs and independent source review; the accepted receipt expressly limits qualification to the selected-target unsigned authoring slice. WU-013 through WU-018 task revision 4 admits only CMakeLists.txt to wire their declared compiled surfaces into the build. A WU-013 source-only binding against the new WU-012 receipt passed locally. A Windows Debug process probe exercised one JSON result, binary framing, request-file input, duplicate/invalid UTF-8 refusal and canary-safe diagnostics. This is source-level behavior for a closed read-only command subset; no TTY acceptance, reconnect after effects, mutation routing or product release qualification is claimed. Independent review of the first WU-013 head found that EOF could mask read failure and buffered response writes could fail after an apparent success; focused failing-stream probes now reject combined bad/EOF and flush failures. A fresh isolated Windows Debug 8,192-file probe measured ownership loading alone at 97,333,248 bytes versus full verification at 97,439,744 bytes. The prior-format reader is the dominant peak; this task revision admits its exact implementation file for a bounded repair. A clean-source Windows Debug follow-up measured separate 128, 4,097 and 8,192-entry reader, verify and uninstall-plan child processes after fixture preparation; the 8,192-entry peaks were 64,434,176, 64,520,192 and 64,630,784 bytes. The result improves the earlier 97 MB shape but does not impose an aggregate allocation budget or qualify full 4,096-entry lifecycle. A source-bound external one-file C product probe compiled outside USK, packaged the actual Debug usk_machine binary into both envelope shapes, reinspected the extracted carrier product graph, and launched the read-only machine command successfully. The carrier requires extraction and has no direct entrypoint. The runtime dependency closure, product install/maintenance path, signing and native publisher remain unqualified. The sidecar manifest uses exclusive creation; a focused competing-writer test confirms a newly created outsider file is not overwritten. The emitted ZIP is now byte-compared to a canonical reconstruction, so a hidden PE prefix or trailing data fails inspection; both sidecar and carrier run the complete WU-012 bundle inspector on emitted bytes. Focused adversarial tests cover those cases. The builder now compares the post-composition inspector result to the input-derived manifest; a focused race test substitutes an independently valid alternate host during inspection and confirms both profiles refuse the changed output.
